name: Dhamma Karuṇā

location.address: 30003 Range Road 93, Youngstown, AB T0J 3P0, Canada

tradition: Vipassana Meditation as taught by S.N. Goenka
technique: Anapana (breath awareness) followed by Vipassana body-scanning meditation, taught in silent, structured ten-day residential courses via recorded instructions and evening discourses from S.N. Goenka
teacherAccess: No individual teacher access; courses are conducted using audio and video recordings of the late S.N. Goenka's instructions and discourses, with certified assistant teachers on site to answer meditation-related questions and give interviews during the rest period.
retreatOptions: Ten-day residential Vipassana courses roughly six times a year (the centre's standard and primary offering), plus 1- to 3-day refresher courses, longer old-student courses (10-day Satipatthana, 20-day and longer, and a 14-day Gratitude course) for qualified students, and one-day children's and teenagers' Anapana courses (ages 8-17).
about: Dhamma Karuṇā, formally the Alberta Vipassana Meditation Centre (AVMC), is the Goenka-tradition Vipassana centre for Alberta, set on 8.5 acres on the outskirts of Youngstown, a small farming village in the Canadian Badlands roughly three to five hours by car from Edmonton, Calgary, Regina, and Saskatoon. The property, a former special-needs school known as the Youngstown Home, was purchased in July 2014 by the nonprofit Alberta Vipassana Foundation as the centre's permanent site. The main building holds a meditation hall for about 80 students, a kitchen, offices, and teacher quarters, while a separate two-storey residence building provides double and single rooms for up to 80 students and servers with eight shared bath areas; additional long-term server housing has been added in a converted garage and a renovated trailer, each with small kitchens and private bathrooms. The centre offers residential ten-day Vipassana courses as taught by S.N. Goenka in the tradition of Sayagyi U Ba Khin roughly six times a year, interspersed with old-student service periods, alongside shorter refresher courses, longer courses for experienced students, and one-day courses for children and teens. Students live on site for the full course, observe Noble Silence, and follow the standard Goenka daily schedule; as at every centre in the Goenka network, there are no fees of any kind - courses, food, and lodging are offered purely on a dana (voluntary donation) basis by past students.
schedule: Standard Goenka ten-day course schedule: arrival and registration from 2-4pm on the start day, followed by ten full days of silent sitting meditation (roughly 4am-9:30pm) with recorded evening discourses, and course close around 7am on the final day followed by breakfast and departure by mid-morning; Noble Silence is observed by all students until the morning of the last full day.
cost: No fees of any kind; entirely dana (voluntary donation)-based, in keeping with the worldwide Goenka Vipassana tradition - all teaching, food, and accommodation are offered freely, funded by donations from past students who have completed at least one prior course.

pricePerDay.notes: No suggested amount; a Goenka-tradition (dhamma.org) course funded entirely by voluntary donation from past students, none of whom - including teachers and organizers - receive any payment for their service.

foodNotes: All meals prepared and served on-site at no charge for the duration of the course; simple vegetarian meals throughout, with old students keeping the no-eating-after-midday precept while new students may have tea with milk and fruit at the evening break.
workNotes: Old students (those who have completed at least one prior ten-day course) may serve courses as Dhamma volunteers or join dedicated old-student work periods for centre maintenance and gardening; new students are not required to work during their first course.
